title: Rav Natan bar Abba (I)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a student of Rav, citing his explanation of a teaching before Rav in [Bava Metzia 41a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.41a.9) and his reports in [Beitzah 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.32b.1-5).
“Rav Natan bar Abba said in the name of Rav.” Three occurrences [ג״פ].

In [Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.2.9.5), Natan bar Ba tells Shmuel: “I know how to distinguish the roe of non-kosher fish from that of kosher fish: the former is round, the latter elongated.” Shmuel shows him a salpita; Natan calls it non-kosher. Shmuel says: “Calling a kosher one non-kosher does not trouble me, but you will end by calling a non-kosher one kosher.” Hyman reports that [Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Avodah_Zarah.40a.13.1), under “Amar Rava”, cites this passage under the name Rav Natan bar Rava. Hyman identifies him as the same person, saying that Rava and Abba are one name.[^1]

notes.text: [Hyman, vol. III, p. 954](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=121) gives the count alongside the formula. The three teachings in Beitzah concern a Festival wick, wealthy Babylonians and reliance on another’s table. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2745&lang=en) also counts three. Bava Metzia gives Rabbi Natan; the Yerushalmi gives Natan bar Ba and the consulted Tosafot gives Natan bar Rava. Hyman’s equation of the names is his interpretation.
